text:
morgan_support: FYI customer 'Maply' opened an urgent ticket — p99 latency shot from ~120ms to 2.3s and some 503s starting ~09:12 UTC. They report timeouts and degraded UX. They pasted their request IDs in the ticket.
lee_oncall: pulling traces + ingress metrics now. Any recent deploys around 09:00–09:15?
olivia_eng: there was a small rollout to the admission-controller yesterday evening but it was staged. nothing scheduled at 09:00 that I recall. will check release notes.
samir_ops: I'm seeing a correlated spike in queue length on the inference pool serving gpt-medium-quantized: queue_depth per-worker went from ~2 to 18 for tenant maply-tenant-id. p95 jumped first, then p99 and a few 503s from admission rejections.
morgan_support: customer says they didn't change traffic pattern; it was steady. we've asked for replay IDs.
lee_oncall: can someone run a quick reproducer with a token from the ticket? try warm + cold to hit cache differences.
olivia_eng: running a local curl against the same model/route with their request payload (sanitized). Reproducer: ```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"long prompt..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=gpt-medium-quantized
```
samir_ops: metrics I queried (PromQL): ```
# per-worker queue depth for tenant
max_over_time(redwood_infer_queue_depth{tenant="maply-tenant-id"}[5m])
# admission rejections
increase(redwood_admission_rejections_total{tenant="maply-tenant-id"}[10m])
``` seeing ~220 rejections starting 09:12.
lee_oncall: logs (snippet) show admission decisions returning reject with reason "concurrency_exceeded" plus a new field "effective_capacity": ```
2026-03-15T09:12:45Z admission-controller INFO tenant=maply-tenant-id decision=reject reason=concurrency_exceeded effective_capacity=2 configured_limit=16
2026-03-15T09:12:46Z worker-17 WARN tenant=maply-tenant-id queue_depth=17 dispatch_delay_ms=2300
```
morgan_support: that effective_capacity=2 looks wrong — configured_limit should be 16. could be a calculation bug? customer-facing impact = many requests hit admission and get 503 or long waits.
olivia_eng: digging into admission-controller diff from last deploy: the change tried to account for pooled-vs-dedicated but a fallback path uses `min(tenant_limit, floor(pool_shares * global_concurrency))` where pool_shares was 0 for tenants without explicit allocation -> floor(...)=0 then we clamp to 2 as a safety lower bound. so some tenants got clamped to 2.
samir_ops: that explains why maply saw effective_capacity=2. But why only surfaced now? maybe traffic pattern slightly higher and cache misses increased. Also model variant moved from gpt-small to gpt-medium-quantized last week which raises per-request GPU usage; combined with clamp it pushed queues.
lee_oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag to disable new clamp logic (fast rollback), 2) increase global safety_clamp to 8, 3) route this tenant to a less-constrained pool / fallback model. We should pick one quick.
morgan_support: customer asked for a short-term work-around; they accept temporary reduced perf if it means fewer errors. prefer routing to a fallback model.
olivia_eng: I can flip the feature flag now (admission.use_new_pool_clamp = false) which will restore previous capacity calc. will post a rollback PR after.
samir_ops: I'm also queuing a routing override to send maply-tenant-id to pool "burst-1" (has spare capacity) for 30m. executing now.
infra-bot: rollout started: feature-flag admission.use_new_pool_clamp -> false by olivia_eng (canary -> all, expected ~20s).
samir_ops: routing override applied for tenant maply-tenant-id -> pool=burst-1 ttl=30m.
lee_oncall: monitoring: queue depth falling. p95 dropping back toward baseline. 503s stopping. keeping watch for 15m.
morgan_support: updated customer: temporary routing + reverted clamp. They confirmed errors dropped and UX mostly recovered, will keep us posted.
olivia_eng: root cause: deployment introduced pool_shares defaulting to 0 for tenants without explicit pool assignments. admission logic used that value and clamped to a low safety floor (2). combination of model variant (higher per-request concurrency) and traffic spike pushed worker queues into backpressure. Fix: 1) change pool_shares default to 1, 2) update clamp to be percentile-based not fixed floor, 3) add tenant-level alert when effective_capacity < configured_limit * 0.25. will send PR with tests.
samir_ops: postmortem action items in ticket: rollback time, routing change, add canary check that compares effective_capacity with configured_limit on deploy, and update runbook to hit fallback model routing earlier.
lee_oncall: closing oncall loop: will keep alert suppression until config patch merges. if anyone wants escalation to infra for dedicated capacity offer for Maply let me know.
morgan_support: ticket updated and customer notified. closing thread once PR merges and we observe stable metrics for 1 hour. thanks all.
